title: Director Business Finance
description: Associate Director Business Finance Location - Bangalore Working Days: 6 Days, In OfficeKey Responsibilities:This role focuses on comprehensive revenue planning rather than cost planning, overseeing the entire conversion journeySummary:Mapping out the lead-to-admission pipeline, from lead generation to sales qualification, initial sales interactions, walk-ins, and finally, admissionsStrategically planning lead generation efforts and allocating the marketing budget based on conversion rates and channel-lead ROIIntegrating marketing and sales budgets to optimize resource and capital deploymentDeveloping and implementing course/product strategies and go-to-market (GTM) interventionsEstablishing sales excellence models and performance tracking systemsConducting root cause analysis (RCA) on planned vs. actual performance across channels, lead sources, and conversion rates (CVR) to identify and implement corrective actionsEnsuring in-depth, detailed visibility of each stage in the funnelResponsibilities1. Annual Operating Plan (AOP) & Monthly Business Planning• Co-own the AOP process with the Business Head, Category Leads, Sales, Marketing, and Finance — from revenue target setting and funnel assumptions to final plan sign-off.• Break annual targets into monthly, weekly, and channel-level plans; own the cascade of targets across all stakeholders and functions.• Run structured Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs) — tracking plan vs. actuals, identifying gaps early, and aligning corrective action owners with clear timelines.• Maintain a live monthly planning tracker across leads, conversions, revenue, and costs — updated and shared proactively.2. Revenue Funnel Planning & Tracking• Own end-to-end visibility of the lead-to-revenue funnel: lead generation → marketing qualified leads (MQLs) → sales qualified leads (SQLs) → trials/demos → conversions → renewals.• Plan lead volumes, conversion rate benchmarks, and revenue outcomes by course, category, channel, and cohort — and hold each stage of the funnel accountable.• Build and maintain dashboards to track funnel health in real time; surface early warning signals before they translate into a revenue miss.3. Sales & Marketing Channel Strategy & Budget Planning• Partner with marketing leads to build channel-wise lead budgets grounded in CPL, channel CVR, and ROI — ensuring spend is performance-linked, not just historical.• Evaluate and recommend reallocation of marketing budgets across channels — scaling high-ROI sources, rationalizing underperformers.• Work with Sales Head to build sales productivity models: revenue target per head, funnel throughput per rep, and team sizing vs. plan.• Integrate marketing and sales budgets into a unified revenue plan — no siloed planning.4. Root Cause Analysis (RCA) — Plan vs. Achievement• Lead structured RCAs whenever revenue deviates from plan — dissecting by channel, lead source, category, funnel stage, cohort, and time period.• Translate RCA findings into corrective actions with named owners, timelines, and success metrics — not just diagnosis, but recovery planning.• Present RCA outputs to Sales Head, Marketing Leads, Category Leads, Academics Head, and Business Head — with solutions, not just slides.• Maintain a living tracker of open RCA actions and their status across functions.5. Course & Category-wise Revenue Strategy• Partner with Category Leads and the Academics Head to build course-level revenue targets, pricing strategies, and GTM intervention plans.• Track category performance: enrollments, revenue per student, dropout rates, renewal rates, and course-level contribution margins.• Build business cases for new course launches or pricing changes, including market sizing, competitive benchmarking, and projected ROI.6. Performance Reporting & Business Intelligence• Own the performance reporting cadence — daily/weekly/monthly — with clear accountability mapped to each KPI.• Build and manage dashboards across revenue, sales productivity, marketing efficiency, and funnel health.• Prepare crisp, insight-driven decks for Business Head and senior leadership reviews — distilling complexity into decision-ready outputs.B. Cost, Headcount & Investment Planning (30%)7. Headcount Planning & Resource Budgeting• Plan and track headcount requirements across sales, marketing, and operations — aligned to revenue targets and per-head productivity benchmarks.• Collaborate with functional heads to build hiring plans, role-level budgets, and cost-per-hire models for the AOP cycle.• Flag headcount risks proactively — over-hiring against a revenue shortfall, or under-hiring against an aggressive plan.8. Marketing Spend Governance & Efficiency• Own marketing budget tracking — planned vs. actual spend by channel, campaign, and period; update in real time.• Monitor marketing efficiency ratios (CAC, CPL, ROAS, payback period) and call out inefficiencies with recommended actions.• Flag budget overruns or reallocation opportunities in real time — do not wait for month-end reviews.9. Course-wise P&L Tracking• Maintain course-level P&L visibility — revenue, direct variable costs, contribution margins, and profitability trends by cohort.• Identify underperforming courses or categories early; propose strategic or operational interventions to course heads and BH.• Ensure P&L data is granular, trusted, and decision-ready — not a backward-looking report, but a forward-looking signal.10. New Investment Evaluation & ROI Tracking• Evaluate business cases for new investments — course launches, technology tools, marketing experiments, and team expansions.• Build financial models and ROI frameworks to support go/no-go decisions; set clear return expectations and payback timelines.• Track post-investment outcomes vs. projections; close the loop with stakeholders and inform future investment decisions.11. Risk Identification, Call-outs & Contingency Planning• Proactively identify financial and operational risks across revenue and cost — and present solutions alongside the flag, not separately.• Develop contingency plans for high-probability scenarios: demand softness, channel saturation, CAC inflation, cost overruns.• Maintain a live risk register with impact assessments, probability ratings, and mitigation owners — reviewed at every MBR.Qualifications● Bachelor & Master degree from tier 1 college● 4+ years of experience in revenue planning, growth planning , conversion/sales strategy business planning, financial analysis, or strategic planning roles.● Strong financial modeling and data analysis skills, with experience in using advanced analytics tools and software.● Proven track record in developing and executing business plans in a corporate environment.● Excellent communication and presentation skills with experience presenting to senior leadership.● Strong project management skills, with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple initiatives.● Strategic thinker with excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

title: Flutter Developer
description:
**About Us**

Scapia! A credit card that's out there to make travel happen for people, by converting their everyday expenses into travel experiences. We're a bunch of passionate people who work together, brainstorm, and debate with each other, and don't stop until we're proud of our work. Customer delight tops everything else! We've worked hard to create an environment of honesty and passion that sets everyone up for success.

**About the Role**

We are looking for Flutter Engineers with 4 to 6 years of experience to join the frontend team at Scapia.You will be placed in a pod based on where your strengths fit. You will work across surfaces spanning card onboarding and servicing, UPI and bill payments, travel

search and checkout, rewards, and the shared design system beneath them. You will collaborate closely with design, backend, product and our bank and supplier partner teams to take a surface from spec through to a staged production rollout.

**What You'll Do**

**Feature Ownership**

* Own customer-facing surfaces end to end, from problem definition and technical design through rollout, adoption metrics and the on-call that follows.
* Set the technical direction for your surface and make the architecture calls that keep it changeable a year from now.
* Partner with design, product and backend to turn ambiguous problem statements into shipped, measured experiences.

**Cards and Payments**

* Build and scale the card experience across onboarding, activation, limits, statements, EMI and rewards.
* Deliver payment experiences that are fast, reliable and compliant, spanning UPI, bill payments and card transactions.
* Shape how the app adapts to multiple bank partners, so that a single change ships safely across every programme.

**Travel Commerce**

* Build high-converting search, booking and checkout journeys across flights, stays, trains, buses, visas and experiences.
* Create discovery and merchandising surfaces that help customers evaluate options and choose with confidence.
* Own post-booking experiences spanning cancellations, refunds, rewards and customer communication.

**App Health and Performance**

* Continuously improve app performance, stability and size across ANRs, crashes, startup time and memory.
* Strengthen observability through crash reporting, instrumentation and analytics that teams can act on.
* Advance release engineering, including staged rollouts, remote kill switches and over-the-air patching on Android and iOS.

**Platform and Craft**

* Contribute to the shared design system and widget library that every surface at Scapia is built on.
* Champion clean architecture, testing and code quality, from golden tests to end-to-end automation.
* Raise the bar for the team through spec reviews, code reviews and the tooling you build along the way.

**How We Build**

Every change here starts as a written spec that is reviewed and approved before implementation begins. AI agents do a lot of the work in between: generating implementation from an approved spec, turning Figma components into design system code, and cleaning up dead feature flags. The review bar has not changed. You own the design, you review the diff, and you answer for it in production.

**What We're Looking For**

* 4 to 6 years of Flutter experience, with at least one app shipped to a store and supported in production.
* Strong Dart fundamentals and real depth in state management with Bloc or Cubit.
* Ability to read a crash report or a trace and work backwards to the cause.
* Clear written communication. Specs, pull request descriptions and incident notes are a large part of the job.
* Comfort with ownership: your own builds, the pager for your surface, and your own production debugging.

**Good to Have**

* Native Android (Kotlin) or iOS (Swift) depth for platform channel work.
* Experience with a shared SDK or a multi-flavour app where one change affects several products.
* Prior experience in fintech, payments, travel or another regulated or transaction-led domain.
* Startup mindset: comfortable with ambiguity, fast iteration, and wearing multiple hats.

title: Game Design & Development Intern (Tactile Games)
description:
uDot is hiring a paid intern to turn our refreshable tactile display into a games platform that blind and visually impaired kids actually want to play.

**About uDot**

uDot Braille Tech builds a refreshable tactile display and a curriculum-aligned learning platform that make science and math accessible to blind and visually impaired school students. Kids explore graphs, shapes and diagrams with their fingertips.

Our goal is one million blind kids growing up STEM-native. The device is already in classrooms. Now we want kids to fight over whose turn it is.

**The role**

You will build uDot's game ecosystem: a library of games, tutorials that teach each game without a sighted helper, a reward system that brings kids back, and sound that makes the device feel like a gaming console, not an assistive aid. We don't yet know which games work best, and we want you to bring ideas we haven't thought of. Finding out what works, with real kids, is the job.

The hard part, and the interesting part: your players can't see. Games are felt on a tactile display and heard through audio, and a tactile display does not behave like a screen. Excitement has to come from sound, timing and clever design, not graphics.

**What you'll do**

* Play with blind kids first. Join school sessions, watch what makes kids lean in and where they get stuck, and talk to the teachers.
* Prototype fast. Get a rough playable version on the device in days, not weeks, using AI coding tools.
* Ship games across genres, including games that sneak in math and science.
* Design the sound: effects, music cues and voice feedback that make a game exciting, not a screen reader reading out a menu.
* Build tutorials into every game, so a child learns to play through touch and sound alone in the first minute.
* Design the ecosystem: levels, streaks, badges, unlockables, leaderboards, and a launcher kids can browse without sight. Build reusable pieces so the next game takes half the time.
* Playtest, track which games kids return to and where they quit, and improve what matters.

**You must have**

Graphics, 3D and animation skills won't matter much here. Game design, sound and fast prototyping will.

* Game design sense: you can explain why a game is fun (rules, core loop, feedback, difficulty, rewards). Extra points if you love board games, puzzles or strategy games and have designed your own.
* Games you've built, digital or physical: game jam entries, web or mobile games, board or card games, puzzles, mods.
* An ear for sound: you can make, find and edit sound effects, and use or want to learn tools such as Audacity, Reaper, FMOD, the Web Audio API and AI audio generators.
* Strong coding, AI-native: you use AI coding tools every day and can still read, debug and fix what they produce.
* Design empathy: you will blindfold yourself to play your own game before anyone else does.
* Comfortable with kids: patient, observant, and able to learn more from watching a 10-year-old play than from a survey.
* Ownership: you work well in a small team and ship without being told every step.
* Full-time, on-site availability for 3–6 months from December 2026 or January 2027.

**Nice to have**

* Audio or accessible games, or screen readers such as TalkBack or NVDA
* Board game, puzzle or toy design
* A game engine such as Unity or Godot
* Game jams (Global Game Jam, GMTK, Ludum Dare and similar)
* Multiplayer games
* Hardware or electronics tinkering
* Educational game design or gamification for learning
* Kannada, Hindi or another Indian language, for school sessions

**Details**

* Paid internship, 3–6 months
* Start December 2026 or January 2027. Final-semester students can intern until their semester ends.
* On-site, Electronic City, Bengaluru (you need the device in your hands every day)
* Open to final-year students and recent graduates from any discipline: CS, design, game design, music or audio tech

**Application challenge**
(about 2–3 hours, no code needed)

We care more about how you think than about your CV. Design an original game for a blind 10-year-old, played on a tactile display (think of a low-resolution black-and-white screen you read with your fingers, which refreshes far slower than a normal display) with audio.

In one to two pages, or a video of up to three minutes, answer:

1. What does the player feel, hear and do, moment to moment?

2. How does the game teach itself, with no adult helping?

3. What makes the child want to play again tomorrow?

4. What is the first thing you would test with real kids, and how?

**Bonus:**
a rough playable prototype that simulates the tactile display on screen, with sound.

**How to apply**

Apply here, then email kaviraj@udot.tech with the subject "Game Intern – Your Name" and include your CV, links to games you've built (playable links first), your challenge response, and your available dates, including your semester end date if you're a final-year student.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

title: Founding Engineer, Builder Experience
description:
Millions of people are about to start building software. Build the experience that gets their work into the world.

**The role**

Picture a finance analyst who has just built something brilliant with an AI agent, on their laptop, over a weekend. Today, that is where it dies. Your job is to make sure it doesn’t. You will own the experience that takes anything anyone builds, with any AI tool, and turns it into real, trusted company software, without them ever needing to become an engineer.

This is developer experience for the next billion builders, and the hardest version of it: your users can’t read a stack trace, so the product has to just work.

**What you’ll own**

* The builder’s journey from “it works on my laptop” to “the whole company uses it”, wherever they build.
* The intelligence that converts apps built anywhere into secure, connected company apps, without breaking what already works.
* How Isomorph guides every builder’s own AI agent, so they get things right without learning any rules.
* A product that gets smarter with every app that passes through it.

**What you’ll get to build next**

* Turn what we learn from every real app into an edge no general-purpose agent has. Over time, that becomes the foundation for models of our own.
* Get to a world where any app goes live in minutes, and builders almost never get stuck.

**You’ll thrive here if**

* You have built developer tools or products that people loved, and you obsess over the first five minutes.
* You are a strong engineer who can understand code you didn’t write, fast.
* You live in AI coding agents and have strong opinions on how to make them reliable.
* You get excited by making something hard feel effortless.

**Why Isomorph**

For fifty years, software inside a company has been written by a small group of engineers, for everyone else. That is ending. With AI, the people who know the work best (the finance analyst, the ops lead, the recruiter, the support manager) can now build the software they need themselves. Most of them have never written a line of code.

This is one of the biggest shifts in how companies work, and it has a missing piece. The software these people build is useful, and very often unsafe: no sign-in, sensitive data exposed, nobody to run it, and invisible to IT. Multiply that across a large company and you get thousands of apps and agents that nobody governs.

**Isomorph is the foundation that software runs on.**
Bring an app or agent built with any AI tool, and Isomorph runs it on the company’s own cloud: secured, connected to company data and systems, monitored and kept healthy. Builders never think about infrastructure. IT stays in control of everything.

We believe every company will become AI-native one workflow at a time, built by its own people. Isomorph is where that software will live.

**The team.**
You will join a small, high-talent-density founding team from IIT Madras and IIT Delhi. The founders are second-time founders who have built companies before and sold one.

**Why you’ll love it here**

* **You’ll be early.**
  You will be one of the first people on the team, with real ownership and a real say in what Isomorph becomes.
* **You’ll work at the frontier.**
  AI agents and enterprise-grade infrastructure, applied to a problem every company is about to have.
* **You’ll see your impact.**
  We work side by side with customers, so what you ship is in real people’s hands within days.
* **You’ll build the way the future builds.**
  We build Isomorph with AI agents ourselves, so your leverage is your judgment and your taste, not your typing speed.
* **You’ll grow fast.**
  Small team, huge surface, founders who have built and scaled before.

Apply: https://isomorph.ai/careers/founding-engineer-builder-experience/

title: Software Development Engineer III
description:
**About the role**

We need strong Java engineers to build high-throughput, low-latency backend services for AI-powered search query understanding and customer personalisation. These services integrate LLMs for query classification and expansion and connect with personalisation systems to make search results increasingly relevant to individual customers. The services must operate at very high scale with strict latency requirements and must be LLM-provider agnostic.
  
**You will be responsible for**
Skill DetailJava (17+) Must have production experience building high-throughput, low-latency services in Java on Spring Boot or equivalent.LLM Integration (Production) Hands-on production experience integrating large language models (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, open-source models) into backend services – including prompt management, structured output parsing, retry/fallback logic, and token-cost optimisation.Prompt Engineering Demonstrated ability to design, version, and evaluate prompts for query understanding, query expansion, and classification tasks. Experience with few-shot, chain-of-thought, and constrained-output prompting patterns.NLP / Information Retrieval Strong grounding in query understanding, query rewriting/expansion, synonym handling, intent classification, and search relevance. Understanding of how query processing pipelines work in e-commerce search.Microservices Architecture Production experience designing stateless, cache-first, horizontally scalable microservices. Familiarity with service extraction patterns.Caching Strategies Experience with distributed caching (Redis, Memcached, or similar) to minimise LLM calls for repeated or similar queries.API Design (RESTful / gRPC) Clean API contract design, versioning, backward compatibility. Services must expose well-defined interfaces for downstream consumers.Personalisation Systems (Production) Demonstrable production experience building or integrating with personalisation engines, recommendation systems, or customer profile/preference platforms. Understanding of explicit vs. implicit preference capture and the feedback loops that drive them.Data Pipeline Engineering Experience building real-time and batch data pipelines for customer event processing (Kafka, Event Hubs, or similar).LLM/Agent Memory & Context Understanding of how to integrate user profile/preference data into LLM agent workflows – prompt injection of user context, session memory management, retrieval-augmented personalisation. Ability to bridge traditional personalisation systems with LLM-based agents.Customer Data Platforms Experience with customer data platforms, identity resolution, and privacy-compliant data handling (GDPR).Cloud Platform (Azure) Production deployment experience on Azure or equivalent.CI/CD & Observability Experience with production CI/CD pipelines, structured logging, distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry or equivalent), and monitoring/alerting for ML-integrated services.
  
  
**You will need**
Desirable SkillsSkill DetailE-commerce Search Prior experience with product search, catalogue search, or retail search systems.Elasticsearch / OpenSearch Understanding of search engine internals, index design, and query DSL.Statistical Analysis & A/B Testing Frameworks Strong statistical skills for A/B test to analyse search relevance improvements, significance testing, confidence intervals, segmentation analysis. Experience with sequential testing or Bayesian approaches is a plus.Model Serving Experience with model serving infrastructure (TensorFlow Serving, TorchServe, vLLM, or managed endpoints).NLP for Preference Extraction Experience using NLP techniques (entity extraction, sentiment analysis) to derive preferences from unstructured text.Feature Stores Experience with feature stores for serving personalisation features at low latency.Privacy Engineering Experience implementing data minimisation, consent management, and right-to-erasure.Grocery Retail Domain Familiarity with grocery retail personalisation – dietary preferences, brand loyalty, promotional sensitivity.
  
Soft Skills & Working Style RequirementsThe following attributes are non-negotiable across all roles. This project operates under an aggressive six-month timeline with high executive visibility. The team must move fast, make pragmatic decisions, and deliver production-quality work without the luxury of extended ramp-up periods.Fungibility & Versatility• Willingness and ability to work across boundaries when needed. Priorities shift in a fast-moving programme and people may be asked to contribute outside their core area.• Comfort with ambiguity – requirements will evolve as we learn from early releases. Contractors must be able to work with incomplete specifications and make sound judgements.• T-shaped skills profile: deep in their primary skill area, but broad enough to contribute meaningfully in adjacent areas.Collaboration & Communication• Proven ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams (engineering, product, design, data science).• Clear, concise communication in English (written and verbal). Must be comfortable in daily stand-ups, design reviews, and sprint ceremonies.• Experience working with distributed/hybrid teams across multiple locations and time zones.• Willingness to pair-programme, do code reviews, and share knowledge actively. No “lone wolf” engineers.Go-Getter / Delivery Mindset• Demonstrable track record of delivering under tight deadlines. We are looking for people who take ownership, unblock themselves, and drive towards outcomes rather than waiting for perfect requirements.• Bias to action: when faced with two reasonable options, pick one and move forward rather than debating endlessly.• Comfort with iterative delivery – ship an MVP, learn, iterate. Not gold-plating.• Proactive communication of risks, blockers, and trade-offs. No surprises.Production Discipline• All contractors must have deployed to production using the core skills listed for their role. PoC / hackathon / side-project experience alone is insufficient.• Strong engineering practices: code review, testing, documentation, observability. Every line of code must be production-grade from day one.• Understanding of and respect for operational concerns: monitoring, alerting, incident response, on-call readiness.Cultural Fit• Customer-first mindset. Every decision should be evaluated through the lens of “does this make the customer experience better?”• Comfort working in a large enterprise environment while maintaining startup-like speed and pragmatism.• Intellectual curiosity about AI/LLM capabilities and their practical application in retail.
  
  
**Whats in it for you?**
  
At Tesco, we are committed to providing the best for you. 
  
 
  
As a result, our colleagues enjoy a unique, differentiated, market- competitive reward package, based on the current industry practices, for all the work they put into serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day.

title: SAP Business AI (Joule and Basic ABAP) - Senior, Tax Technology Services
description:
**Summary**
**Position Summary**
**SAP Business AI (Joule and Basic ABAP) - Senior, Tax Technology Services**
Deloitte Tax Services India Private Limited (“USI Tax”) commenced operations in June 2004. Since then, nearly all the Deloitte Tax LLP (“Deloitte Tax”) U.S. service offerings have obtained support services through the USI Tax teams. USI Tax offers you opportunities to learn and support U.S. and other countries (such as Australia, Belgium, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom) taxation practice, a popular career option.
  
  
Deloitte Tax is leading its clients through the tax transformation taking place in the marketplace, offering a broad range of fully integrated tax services by combining technology and technical tax resources to comply with reporting requirements, uncover insights and deploy smarter approaches for navigating an increasingly complex global environment.
  
  
**Work you’ll do**
We are looking for an innovative Technical SAP ABAP on HANA, CDS, OData, RAP Plus Gen AI develop and implement systems architecture that meet business needs, along with ensuring that our clients’ can keep pace with the changing tax and legal landscape.
  
  
Design, build, and support performance SAP S/4HANA extensions and services using ABAP on HANA, RESTful ABAP Programming Model (RAP), Core Data Services (CDS), and OData to enable modern Fiori/UI and integration scenarios.
  
  
To be successful in this role, you should be able to align the global Tax and Legal landscape with the business’ activities and proposed wider business processes. You will be the lynchpin between the Tax Function and IT Function, ensuring that we build the best SAP Tax design for the client. This will require the ability to explain complex terms to a variety of different stakeholders, and in a way that is relevant to each stakeholder group. You will also need to continually assess the SAP product suite and development roadmap to integrate any updated specifications and requirements into SAP system architecture.
  
  
You will also need to integrate with the wider client project team (whether that is delivered by Deloitte Consulting or another Systems Integration partner). This will involve an understanding of how the tax design interacts with other process flows and also the inter-personal skills to build the required relationships.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities -**

* Develop and enhance ABAP solutions on SAP S/4HANA using clean, modular, and testable patterns.
* Build Gen AI applications and AI Agents.
* Code Python is a plus.
* Ability to navigate fragmented landscapes through API-calls and MCP- servers is key.
* Build end-to-end RAP artifacts (behavior definitions/implementations, validations, determinations, actions, draft handling, locking, authorization concepts).
* Create and optimize CDS views (interface/consumption views, associations, annotations) with strong focus on pushdown and performance.
* Design, expose, and support OData services (preferably OData V4 via RAP; maintain OData V4 where required).
* Implement Fiori-enablement via CDS annotations and support UI integration with SAP Fiori elements (as applicable).
* Integrate with SAP and non-SAP systems using SAP-recommended patterns (e.g., APIs, events, messaging where applicable).

* Produce technical designs, code documentation, unit tests, and participate in code reviews.
* Support testing cycles, defect triage, hyper care, and production support with strong root-cause analysis

* 4+ years of Experience in SAP or SAP4HANA.
* Hands-on experience in building Gen AI applications, AI Agents.

* SAP certifications (ABAP for S/4HANA, RAP, BTP) are a plus.
* Strong hands-on experience with ABAP in SAP S/4HANA / ABAP on HANA environments.
* Proven delivery experience with:
* RAP (managed/unmanaged as needed, behavior implementation, draft, authorization)
* CDS (views, annotations, associations, table functions if needed)
* OData service exposure and troubleshooting (RAP/OData V4 strongly preferred)
* Strong understanding of HANA-optimized development: SQL/CDS pushdown, avoiding SELECT-in-loops, efficient joins, pagination, etc.
* Familiarity with modern ABAP practices (e.g., ABAP OO, clean code, exception handling, unit testing mindset).
* Experience working in Agile delivery (user stories, estimation, sprint ceremonies).

**Preferred / Nice To Have**

* SAP BTP exposure (e.g., Integration Suite, API Management, Event Mesh, ABAP environment/Steampunk—if relevant).

title: Chief AI/ML Architect
description:
Overview of 66degrees
  
  
66degrees is an end-to-end AI transformation partner that guides enterprises from complex business challenges to clear, quantifiable outcomes. Our company is the culmination of several successful firms, each a leader in its own right in cloud, artificial intelligence, and data. This convergence of talent and expertise is how we help businesses reach their own "inflection point," where chaotic data becomes a strategic asset, complexity becomes clarity, and AI becomes an engine for growth. Our ultimate vision is to be the catalyst for a future where every business operates as an intelligent enterprise, with autonomous systems unlocking human potential.
  
  
At 66degrees, we believe in thriving through challenges and winning together. These values not only guide us in achieving our goals as a company but also for our people. We are dedicated to creating a significant impact for our employees by fostering a culture that sparks innovation and supports professional and personal growth along the way.
  
  
Overview of Role
  
  
An AI/ML Architect at 66degrees designs and ships production AI systems for enterprise clients and leads the engineers who build them. The Architect is the senior technical person on an engagement: the primary technical point of contact for the client, the owner of the architecture, and the person the team takes direction from.
  
  
The role is hands-on and client-facing in equal measure. Architects take a business problem, define the solution and the value it delivers, and then build and deploy it. They write and review code, make the architectural decisions, and stay with the system through production. They also run discovery, present to client executives, and are the face of 66degrees on the engagement.
  
  
This role is based in India and works daily with US-based colleagues and clients. Engagements typically run 12 to 16 weeks and are delivered by a Delivery Manager, one or more Architects, and a team of engineers.
  
  
Why this role
  
  

* 2026 Google Cloud AI Partner of the Year. This team's work won the Artificial Intelligence category this year, one of four Partner of the Year awards 66degrees has earned. You're joining the top of the Google Cloud AI ecosystem
* About 60% of the work is generative and agentic AI, in production, for clients up to the Fortune 10. The rest is classical ML and MLOps, so you build real agents without losing the rest of the craft.
* New problem, new client, every 12 to 16 weeks. You build range fast and never spend three years on one system
* The whole stack. Architects span infrastructure, software, data, ML, AI, and analytics. The role is built to make you a well-rounded technologist, not to keep you in one lane
* Player-coach all the way up. Growth here doesn't mean giving up the craft. Leaders still build, and the management track is open because the team keeps growing, not because someone has to leave
* No up-or-out, no partner-track politics. Nobody is competing to differentiate themselves; everyone is trying to be the best technologist in the room, which is why people share what they know
* The team has grown roughly tenfold in three years and people stay. The few who've left went on to top tech firms and AI startups

**Responsibilities**
Build
  
  

* Design the architecture for each engagement: data pipelines, classical ML, agentic and generative AI, and the production path on Google Cloud, with the trade-offs written down
* Write and review the code that matters: core logic, orchestration, evaluation, the parts an engineer shouldn't be guessing at
* Take systems to production and own them through handoff: deployment, monitoring, drift, retraining, incident response, and a client who can run it after we leave
* Choose the right approach for the problem, and defend it on cost, explainability, and fit rather than on what's fashionable

Lead the team
  
  

* Direct a team of engineers: write the brief with the reasoning, not only the tasks; confirm it landed before code is written; review the work
* Run a team where engineers raise problems early and are heard when they do
* Develop engineers: pairing, giving them the client call, making them present the design review, and telling the Delivery Manager who is ready for more
* Delegate real work and still own the hard parts. Not a solo builder; not a delegator who only checks in

Own the client relationship
  
  

* Run discovery: turn an ambiguous ask into a scoped plan with success criteria the client agrees to
* Hold the solution to what the client actually needs, and when scope and need diverge, raise it early with options and what each costs
* Raise risk the day you see it, up and across, in business terms, with options. Report "on track" only when it is
* Present to client executives: the design, the trade-offs, the status, and the recommendation, answer first
* Spot expansion: where the client's next problem is, and tell sales

**Qualifications**
Technical (required)
  
  

* Has personally designed and shipped production ML or AI systems, more than once, and owned them after launch. This is a hard requirement: an Architect who cannot point to systems they built and ran is not an Architect, whatever else is on the resume
* A data science foundation with range: several technique families (classification, forecasting, NLP, deep learning, recommendation, anomaly detection) each tied to a real business outcome. Depth in a few, breadth across the rest
* Has built a generative or agentic AI system that real users depended on: the architecture end to end, where the tools ran, how cost and latency were handled, and how quality was measured. A serious RAG system or single-agent workflow with real evaluation discipline qualifies; a chatbot demo does not
* Production fluency on a hyperscaler: Google Cloud preferred (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Run or GKE); deep AWS or Azure experience with a credible translation is acceptable
* Strong software engineering: expert Python and SQL, containers, CI/CD, and the habits that make code someone else can run
* Currently hands-on, with recent, specific examples of code written and architectural decisions made

Leadership and delivery (required)
  
  

* Currently leads a team of engineers or data scientists, delegating real work while owning the architecture and core logic
* A repeatable method for taking an engagement from discovery through handoff: phases, milestones, who does what, validation before anything ships
* A track record of reshaping scope when the original ask wasn't the right solution, and of making the business case for the change

Communication and judgment (required)
  
  

* Answers the question asked, first, then the detail. Adjusts depth for the audience: can explain a system to an engineer and to a CFO in the same hour
* Executive presence: speaks with conviction, holds a position under challenge, and is someone we would put in front of a client executive next week without coaching
* Raises risk before it becomes a problem, to the person who can act on it, with a proposed fix. Comfortable disagreeing with senior people when the work calls for it
* Comfortable operating with autonomy across a significant time-zone gap with US colleagues and clients

Education
  
  

* Bachelor's degree in computer science, data science, engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience

**Preferred**

* Consulting or professional services background, with fluency in SoWs, scope, and billable delivery
* Google Cloud certifications, or delivery alongside Google teams
* Experience with agentic frameworks and patterns in production: tool calling, state management, MCP, multi-step orchestration, policy-guarded loops

title: Computer Vision Engineer
description:
**Perception Engineer — Computer Vision (UAV)**

SKEYEBOTS | Bengaluru, India | Full-Time | 2–3 years | Immediate joiners prioritised

**About SKEYEBOTS**

SKEYEBOTS builds AI-driven autonomous systems for unmanned platforms across aerial, ground and maritime environments, where perception failures are not an option.

**Role Overview**

We are hiring a Perception Engineer with 4-6 years of experience to build the sensing stack that lets our UAVs see and understand their surroundings, using cameras, LiDAR and radar. You will take perception models and pipelines from research prototypes to reliable, real-time systems running on board drones in flight. You will also build the visual interfaces operators use to monitor them.

This is an immediate opening. Candidates who can join right away will be prioritised.

**At a Glance**

Title: Perception Engineer — Computer Vision

Experience: 4-6 years (industry or post-Master’s research)

Location: Bengaluru, India (on-site; lab and flight testing, with travel as required)

Employment: Full-time

Reports to: Perception Lead

Team: UAV autonomy. You’ll work closely with state estimation, flight control, planning, controls, UI, and hardware.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Design, train, and deploy models for aerial 2D/3D object detection, segmentation, and tracking from camera, LiDAR, and radar data.
* Design and implement classical computer vision algorithms for real-time flight: visual odometry, SLAM, feature matching and optical flow.
* Build radar perception: process mmWave/FMCW radar data (range–Doppler maps, point clouds, CFAR detection) for detection and tracking in low visibility.
* Build multi-sensor fusion pipelines (camera–radar, camera–LiDAR, visual–inertial) for robust scene understanding in flight.
* Develop perception for UAV autonomy: obstacle detection and avoidance, landing-zone detection, terrain mapping, and detect-and-avoid of other aircraft.
* Own sensor calibration and time synchronisation across camera, radar, LiDAR and IMU, including vibration and motion effects on board. Work with the hardware and controls teams on camera and sensor selection.
* Optimise models and CV pipelines for real-time inference on size-, weight- and power-limited edge hardware (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson) using TensorRT, quantisation and profiling for latency, memory and power.
* Integrate perception into the ROS 2 and PX4/ArduPilot stack with clean interfaces to estimation and planning. This covers sensor drivers, message pipelines, custom nodes, and vision-aided navigation and state estimation on PX4.
* Write performance-critical code in C++, and prototype and validate algorithms in Python.
* Contribute to QML/Qt-based UI/HMI components for visualising detections, telemetry overlays, and operator dashboards.
* Build data workflows: flight data collection, labelling guidelines, dataset curation and versioning.
* Define metrics and run evaluations (mAP, IoU, MOTA, latency) in simulation (Gazebo/SITL), on flight logs, and in field trials. Debug failures on real flights.
* Write unit and integration tests and maintain CI pipelines for perception modules.

**Required Qualifications**

* B.Tech/M.Tech/MS in Computer Science, Electronics, Aerospace, Robotics, or a related field.
* 4-6 years building computer vision or perception systems, with at least one system deployed on real hardware (UAV preferred).
* Strong Python and modern C++ (C++14/17), including writing performance-critical code.
* Hands-on deep learning with PyTorch: training, fine-tuning, and evaluating detection or segmentation models.
* Working knowledge of radar signal processing: FMCW principles, range–Doppler–angle estimation, CFAR and clustering.
* Solid grounding in multi-view geometry and CV fundamentals: camera models, calibration, projections, epipolar geometry, feature detection, optical flow, and 3D coordinate transforms. Hands-on with OpenCV.
* Working experience with ROS or ROS 2 (nodes, topics, services, tf/tf2, launch files).
* Experience with multi-sensor fusion and tracking (Kalman filters, data association).
* Comfortable with Linux, Git, and debugging on embedded or flight hardware.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Hands-on with PX4 or ArduPilot, MAVLink, offboard control, and flight testing (awareness of DGCA drone rules is a plus).
* Experience with automotive/aerial mmWave radars (e.g., TI AWR/IWR series) and radar–camera fusion models.
* Deep-learning-based radar perception on raw ADC data, radar cubes, or radar point clouds.
* Deployment with TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, or CUDA on Jetson-class devices, or other NPUs.
* Exposure to visual-inertial odometry or SLAM (VINS-Fusion, ORB-SLAM, RTAB-Map, factor graphs) for GPS-denied flight.
* Experience building UI components with QML/Qt.
* Multi-modal sensor fusion including thermal/IR alongside RGB, stereo/depth and LiDAR, plus IMU and GPS fusion.
* Familiarity with simulators (AirSim, Isaac Sim, Gazebo, jMAVSim), SITL/HITL, and synthetic aerial data generation.
* Experience with TensorFlow in addition to PyTorch.
* Experience setting up CI pipelines and test frameworks for perception or robotics software.
* Publications at robotics, vision or radar venues (ICRA, IROS, CVPR, RA-L, IEEE RadarConf) or strong open-source contributions.

**Tools and Tech Stack**

Languages: Python, C++17, CUDA (plus), MATLAB (plus)

Deep learning: PyTorch, TensorFlow (plus), ONNX, TensorRT

Vision and 3D: OpenCV, Open3D, PCL

Radar: mmWave/FMCW radar SDKs, range–Doppler processing, CFAR, DBSCAN

UAV and robotics: ROS 2, PX4 / ArduPilot, MAVLink, AirSim / Gazebo / jMAVSim, SITL/HITL

UI: Qt / QML

Sensors: RGB, thermal and stereo cameras, mmWave radar, 3D LiDAR, IMU, GNSS

Hardware: NVIDIA Jetson Orin, flight controllers (Pixhawk), GPU workstations

Infra: Linux, Docker, Git, CI, experiment tracking (W&B or MLflow)

**What We Offer**

* Ownership of perception modules running on real robots, from design to field deployment. Your work goes into real, operational autonomous systems, not just simulation.
* Direct collaboration with the autonomy, controls, and hardware teams on deployed platforms.
* Access to a well-equipped robotics lab, sensor rigs, and GPU compute.
* Mentorship from senior researchers and engineers, with support to publish and attend conferences.
* Competitive compensation + ESOP allocation, health insurance and a learning budget.
* A fast track to greater ownership as the perception team scales.

**How to Apply**

Apply via LinkedIn Easy Apply. In your note, briefly describe a CV or perception problem you solved on a real robotic platform and what made it hard. We review applications on a rolling basis and move quickly.

SKEYEBOTS is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate candidates solely on capability, experience, and drive.

title: Chief AI/ML Architect
description:
Overview of 66degrees
  
  
66degrees is an end-to-end AI transformation partner that guides enterprises from complex business challenges to clear, quantifiable outcomes. Our company is the culmination of several successful firms, each a leader in its own right in cloud, artificial intelligence, and data. This convergence of talent and expertise is how we help businesses reach their own "inflection point," where chaotic data becomes a strategic asset, complexity becomes clarity, and AI becomes an engine for growth. Our ultimate vision is to be the catalyst for a future where every business operates as an intelligent enterprise, with autonomous systems unlocking human potential.
  
  
At 66degrees, we believe in thriving through challenges and winning together. These values not only guide us in achieving our goals as a company but also for our people. We are dedicated to creating a significant impact for our employees by fostering a culture that sparks innovation and supports professional and personal growth along the way.
  
  
Overview of Role
  
  
An AI/ML Architect at 66degrees designs and ships production AI systems for enterprise clients and leads the engineers who build them. The Architect is the senior technical person on an engagement: the primary technical point of contact for the client, the owner of the architecture, and the person the team takes direction from.
  
  
The role is hands-on and client-facing in equal measure. Architects take a business problem, define the solution and the value it delivers, and then build and deploy it. They write and review code, make the architectural decisions, and stay with the system through production. They also run discovery, present to client executives, and are the face of 66degrees on the engagement.
  
  
This role is based in India and works daily with US-based colleagues and clients. Engagements typically run 12 to 16 weeks and are delivered by a Delivery Manager, one or more Architects, and a team of engineers.
  
  
Why this role
  
  

* 2026 Google Cloud AI Partner of the Year. This team's work won the Artificial Intelligence category this year, one of four Partner of the Year awards 66degrees has earned. You're joining the top of the Google Cloud AI ecosystem
* About 60% of the work is generative and agentic AI, in production, for clients up to the Fortune 10. The rest is classical ML and MLOps, so you build real agents without losing the rest of the craft.
* New problem, new client, every 12 to 16 weeks. You build range fast and never spend three years on one system
* The whole stack. Architects span infrastructure, software, data, ML, AI, and analytics. The role is built to make you a well-rounded technologist, not to keep you in one lane
* Player-coach all the way up. Growth here doesn't mean giving up the craft. Leaders still build, and the management track is open because the team keeps growing, not because someone has to leave
* No up-or-out, no partner-track politics. Nobody is competing to differentiate themselves; everyone is trying to be the best technologist in the room, which is why people share what they know
* The team has grown roughly tenfold in three years and people stay. The few who've left went on to top tech firms and AI startups

**Responsibilities**
Build
  
  

* Design the architecture for each engagement: data pipelines, classical ML, agentic and generative AI, and the production path on Google Cloud, with the trade-offs written down
* Write and review the code that matters: core logic, orchestration, evaluation, the parts an engineer shouldn't be guessing at
* Take systems to production and own them through handoff: deployment, monitoring, drift, retraining, incident response, and a client who can run it after we leave
* Choose the right approach for the problem, and defend it on cost, explainability, and fit rather than on what's fashionable

Lead the team
  
  

* Direct a team of engineers: write the brief with the reasoning, not only the tasks; confirm it landed before code is written; review the work
* Run a team where engineers raise problems early and are heard when they do
* Develop engineers: pairing, giving them the client call, making them present the design review, and telling the Delivery Manager who is ready for more
* Delegate real work and still own the hard parts. Not a solo builder; not a delegator who only checks in

Own the client relationship
  
  

* Run discovery: turn an ambiguous ask into a scoped plan with success criteria the client agrees to
* Hold the solution to what the client actually needs, and when scope and need diverge, raise it early with options and what each costs
* Raise risk the day you see it, up and across, in business terms, with options. Report "on track" only when it is
* Present to client executives: the design, the trade-offs, the status, and the recommendation, answer first
* Spot expansion: where the client's next problem is, and tell sales

**Qualifications**
Technical (required)
  
  

* Has personally designed and shipped production ML or AI systems, more than once, and owned them after launch. This is a hard requirement: an Architect who cannot point to systems they built and ran is not an Architect, whatever else is on the resume
* A data science foundation with range: several technique families (classification, forecasting, NLP, deep learning, recommendation, anomaly detection) each tied to a real business outcome. Depth in a few, breadth across the rest
* Has built a generative or agentic AI system that real users depended on: the architecture end to end, where the tools ran, how cost and latency were handled, and how quality was measured. A serious RAG system or single-agent workflow with real evaluation discipline qualifies; a chatbot demo does not
* Production fluency on a hyperscaler: Google Cloud preferred (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Run or GKE); deep AWS or Azure experience with a credible translation is acceptable
* Strong software engineering: expert Python and SQL, containers, CI/CD, and the habits that make code someone else can run
* Currently hands-on, with recent, specific examples of code written and architectural decisions made

Leadership and delivery (required)
  
  

* Currently leads a team of engineers or data scientists, delegating real work while owning the architecture and core logic
* A repeatable method for taking an engagement from discovery through handoff: phases, milestones, who does what, validation before anything ships
* A track record of reshaping scope when the original ask wasn't the right solution, and of making the business case for the change

Communication and judgment (required)
  
  

* Answers the question asked, first, then the detail. Adjusts depth for the audience: can explain a system to an engineer and to a CFO in the same hour
* Executive presence: speaks with conviction, holds a position under challenge, and is someone we would put in front of a client executive next week without coaching
* Raises risk before it becomes a problem, to the person who can act on it, with a proposed fix. Comfortable disagreeing with senior people when the work calls for it
* Comfortable operating with autonomy across a significant time-zone gap with US colleagues and clients

Education
  
  

* Bachelor's degree in computer science, data science, engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience

**Preferred**

* Consulting or professional services background, with fluency in SoWs, scope, and billable delivery
* Google Cloud certifications, or delivery alongside Google teams
* Experience with agentic frameworks and patterns in production: tool calling, state management, MCP, multi-step orchestration, policy-guarded loops
* Regulated-industry delivery (financial services, healthcare) where explainability and audit are requirements, not features
* Daily use of AI coding assistants and agents in your own work, with a view on where they help and where they get in the way
* Experience working with a US-based team from India, and a point of view on how to make it work

What the job demands
  
  

* The client sees you. You present the design, you deliver the bad news, you defend the recommendation. The strength of the 66degrees brand on an engagement is the Architect leading it
* The plan will be wrong sometimes. Client problems rarely arrive fully defined, and scope moves. Working out what's really needed and saying so is the job, not an exception to it
* Your engineers learn from you. If you raise risks, they will. If you don't, they won't. You set the standard for how the India team works
* The US is asleep for half your day. You will make decisions with incomplete direction and own them. This role works a shifted schedule: online through 2:00 PM US Eastern (11:30 PM IST), so that most of the US working day overlaps with yours
* It's hands-on. If your week has become meetings and status calls, this is not the role

**About 66degrees And The AI/ML Practice**
66degrees is a leading consulting and professional services company specializing in developing AI-focused, data-led solutions leveraging the latest advancements in cloud technology. With our unmatched engineering capabilities and vast industry experience, we help the world's leading brands transform their business challenges into opportunities and shape the future of work.
  
  
At 66degrees, we believe in embracing the challenge and winning together. These values not only guide us in achieving our goals as a company but also for our people. We are dedicated to creating a significant impact for our employees by fostering a culture that sparks innovation and supports professional and personal growth along the way.
  
  
The AI/ML practice spans roughly 100 specialists across the U.S., Canada, the UK, France, and India, working across three pillars: agentic and generative AI; classical ML; and MLOps and AgentOps. The India team is being built to own engagements end to end, with a path from Engineer to Architect that runs through India.
  
  
***Please note, we cannot sponsor or transfer any visas, of any kind, at this time.***
*66degrees is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, national origin, age, weight, height, marital status, sexual orientation, veteran status, disability status or other legally protected class.*
**AI Transparency & Disclosure**
As an AI transformation partner, 66degrees leverages intelligent solutions to enhance our recruitment experience. We utilize AI tools—including LinkedIn Recruiter’s Hiring Assistant and interview transcription technologies—to assist with sourcing, role analysis, and capturing interview highlights.
  
  
These tools augment our process, but we "Commit to Our Craft" by ensuring all final hiring decisions are made by our human Talent Team. By applying, you acknowledge the use of these technologies to help us "Win Together" in finding the best fit for our team.

- Understanding of machine learning fundamentals, data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model evaluation.

- Experience with RAG pipelines, embeddings, vector databases, and semantic search.

What You'll Gain

- Practical exposure to AWS cloud services and enterprise AI architectures.

- Opportunities to work on industry-focused AI proof-of-concepts and automation solutions.

- Experience taking AI ideas from experimentation to functional prototypes.

title: Founding Engineer, Builder Experience
description:
Millions of people are about to start building software. Build the experience that gets their work into the world.

**The role**

Picture a finance analyst who has just built something brilliant with an AI agent, on their laptop, over a weekend. Today, that is where it dies. Your job is to make sure it doesn’t. You will own the experience that takes anything anyone builds, with any AI tool, and turns it into real, trusted company software, without them ever needing to become an engineer.

This is developer experience for the next billion builders, and the hardest version of it: your users can’t read a stack trace, so the product has to just work.

**What you’ll own**

* The builder’s journey from “it works on my laptop” to “the whole company uses it”, wherever they build.
* The intelligence that converts apps built anywhere into secure, connected company apps, without breaking what already works.
* How Isomorph guides every builder’s own AI agent, so they get things right without learning any rules.
* A product that gets smarter with every app that passes through it.

**What you’ll get to build next**

* Turn what we learn from every real app into an edge no general-purpose agent has. Over time, that becomes the foundation for models of our own.
* Get to a world where any app goes live in minutes, and builders almost never get stuck.

**You’ll thrive here if**

* You have built developer tools or products that people loved, and you obsess over the first five minutes.
* You are a strong engineer who can understand code you didn’t write, fast.
* You live in AI coding agents and have strong opinions on how to make them reliable.
* You get excited by making something hard feel effortless.

**Why Isomorph**

For fifty years, software inside a company has been written by a small group of engineers, for everyone else. That is ending. With AI, the people who know the work best (the finance analyst, the ops lead, the recruiter, the support manager) can now build the software they need themselves. Most of them have never written a line of code.

This is one of the biggest shifts in how companies work, and it has a missing piece. The software these people build is useful, and very often unsafe: no sign-in, sensitive data exposed, nobody to run it, and invisible to IT. Multiply that across a large company and you get thousands of apps and agents that nobody governs.

**Isomorph is the foundation that software runs on.**
Bring an app or agent built with any AI tool, and Isomorph runs it on the company’s own cloud: secured, connected to company data and systems, monitored and kept healthy. Builders never think about infrastructure. IT stays in control of everything.

We believe every company will become AI-native one workflow at a time, built by its own people. Isomorph is where that software will live.

**The team.**
You will join a small, high-talent-density founding team from IIT Madras and IIT Delhi. The founders are second-time founders who have built companies before and sold one.

**Why you’ll love it here**

* **You’ll be early.**
  You will be one of the first people on the team, with real ownership and a real say in what Isomorph becomes.
* **You’ll work at the frontier.**
  AI agents and enterprise-grade infrastructure, applied to a problem every company is about to have.
* **You’ll see your impact.**
  We work side by side with customers, so what you ship is in real people’s hands within days.
* **You’ll build the way the future builds.**
  We build Isomorph with AI agents ourselves, so your leverage is your judgment and your taste, not your typing speed.
* **You’ll grow fast.**
  Small team, huge surface, founders who have built and scaled before.

Apply: https://isomorph.ai/careers/founding-engineer-builder-experience/

title: Engineering Leader
description:
**About Ema**
Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Employees take on the busy work across the employee experience, from recruiting, onboarding and benefits to IT support, invoice processing and payroll, so people can spend their time on work that needs them. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs.
  
  
We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.
  
  
**The Role**
We are looking for an Engineering Leader to manage and scale multiple product lines in the Voice, BPO, and Workforce Management space. This is a high-impact leadership role that sits at the intersection of real-time voice systems, operations research, and data-intensive platform engineering.
  
  
You will report directly to the Head of Engineering and own the engineering organization that builds the infrastructure powering Ema’s Voice AI Employees, Agent QA, auto-learning pipelines, rich analytics, and workforce optimization capabilities — all operating as scalable, multi-tenant systems deployed across global geographies.
  
  
You will collaborate with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to translate customer needs into production systems that handle high volumes of voice data, deliver real-time insights, and continuously improve through automated learning loops. As the owner of multiple product lines, you will balance roadmap priorities across Voice, BPO operations, and WFM (work force management) — ensuring each product evolves cohesively while meeting distinct customer needs.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
**Scalable Multi-Tenant Systems**

* Architect and build multi-tenant systems that serve enterprise customers across geographies with strict data residency, isolation, and compliance requirements.
* Design high-throughput ingestion systems capable of processing large volumes of voice data, call metadata, and operational telemetry in near real-time.
* Make foundational architectural decisions on data stores, stream processing, and storage tiers — balancing query performance, cost, and operational simplicity.
* Champion SOLID principles, clean architecture, and engineering rigor across all codebases — ensuring systems are testable, extensible, and maintainable at scale.

**Team Building & Engineering Culture**

* Recruit, hire, and develop senior engineers across a multi-disciplinary function spanning voice engineering, backend systems, data engineering, and applied operations research.
* Establish engineering standards, code review culture, and a strong bias toward shipping — with equal commitment to system reliability and customer experience.
* Coach and grow senior/staff engineers into technical leaders; manage engineering managers as the organization scales.
* Drive cross-functional alignment with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to ensure the platform evolves in lockstep with customer needs and market feedback.

**Voice Platform & Agent QA**

* Own the end-to-end engineering for Ema’s AgentQA capabilities — real-time voice pipelines, telephony integrations, and voice-to-action workflows.
* Build and scale the Agent QA platform: automated call scoring, compliance monitoring, sentiment analysis, and coaching feedback loops.
* Design auto-learning systems that continuously improve voice agents from production interactions — closed-loop feedback, model retraining triggers, and quality regression detection.
* Deliver rich voice analytics: call volume trends, handle time distributions, first-call resolution metrics, agent performance dashboards, and anomaly detection.
* Build scalable voice pipeline across geographies – keeping in mind PII, security and compliance requirements.

**Workforce Management & Operations Research**

* Build WFM capabilities including demand forecasting, shift scheduling, real-time adherence monitoring, and capacity planning — applying operations research techniques to optimize workforce utilization.
* Design and implement optimization algorithms for headcount modeling, skill-based routing, and workload balancing across multi-site, multi-timezone contact center operations.
* Partner with ML/AI teams to integrate predictive models for call volume forecasting, attrition risk, and staffing efficiency.

**Required**
**What We Look For**

* 12+ years of software engineering experience, with 4+ years leading engineering teams of 8+ engineers at high-growth startups or top-tier tech companies.
* Deep expertise in building real-time, data-intensive systems.

title: Assistant Professor- AI/ML
description:
**About Newton School of Technology (NST)**

Newton School of Technology (NST) is a new-age institution redefining technical education in India. Founded by IIT alumni, NST offers a 4-year B.Tech in Computer Science and AI, focused on hands-on learning and deep industry integration. The program is delivered across

state-of-the-art residential campuses in collaboration with its UGC-recognised partner

universities:

and Silicon Valley. Led by a distinguished faculty comprising ICPC World Finalists and

ex-professionals from ISRO, Microsoft, MakeMyTrip, and several other leading tech organizations, NST is building a scalable, high-impact model that produces industry-ready talent for the world’s most advanced technology roles.

We are currently looking for an Assistant Professor to join our Computer Science Department.

This role is ideal for academic professionals with substantial industry experience or tech

professionals with advanced technical qualifications who are passionate about Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. The position combines hands-on technical expertise with academic responsibilities, including designing and delivering course content, conducting practical lab sessions, and mentoring students in core Data Science and AI/ML concepts.

**Key Responsibilities**

**● Teach Applied AI/ML:**
Design and deliver practical, project-based courses in AI/ML (Python for ML, Statistics, ML Algorithms, Deep Learning, NLP, CV, ML Ops, GenAI).

**● Develop Industry-Relevant Curriculum:**
Help design and update the AI/ML curriculum to reflect current industry tools, techniques, and best practices, incorporating your professional experience and case studies.

**● Mentor Student Projects:**
Guide students through hands-on AI/ML projects, providing technical direction, code reviews, and feedback based on industry standards.

**● Guide & Mentor Students:**
Advise students on developing practical skills, understanding career paths in AI/ML, and preparing for internships and job placements.

**● Stay Current:**
Bring the latest AI/ML research, tools, and industry trends into the classroom.

**● Collaborate:**
Work closely with other expert faculty and staff to create a unified and effective learning experience.

**● Assess Practical Skills:**
Design and evaluate assignments, projects, and assessments

focused on real-world applications.

**Qualifications and Requirements**

**● Mandatory Academic Qualification:**
An M.Tech or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, AI/ML, Engineering, or a strictly related quantitative field is mandatory.

●
**Professional Experience:**
2-10 years of direct, hands-on professional experience in the tech industry as an AI/ML Engineer, Data Scientist, Research Scientist, or a similar role involving AI/ML development and deployment.

**● Proven Industry Track Record:**
Demonstrated experience in building, training, and deploying machine learning models (including deep learning) for real-world problems.

**Required Skills**

**Technical Skills**

● Expert-level Python programming.

● Proficiency with data science libraries (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn).

● Hands-on experience with ML/DL frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch).

● Understanding of ML Ops practices and tools (Git, Docker, AWS/GCP/Azure).

● Knowledge of key AI areas (NLP, Computer Vision, Generative AI/LLMs).

**Soft Skills**

● Strong communication, mentoring ability, collaboration, and a genuine passion for education.

**Good-to-Have**

● Prior teaching experience at the undergraduate or graduate level.

● Familiarity with modern teaching methodologies and academic tools.

title: Social Media Manager
description:

With services across 17+ global markets and expanding rapidly across Europe, Asia, and North America, we pride ourselves on delivering clean clothes within 24 hours, making us one of the fastest services in the business.
  
  
We are looking for a
**Social Media Specialist to own and grow Laundryheap's presence across social platforms in our international markets.**
This role focuses on performance-driven social content, short-form video and creator partnerships that build reach, engagement and brand visibility.
  
  
This is a hands-on role responsible for planning, creating, publishing and measuring social content, working closely with the Content, Brand, Design, Growth and Paid teams.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Social Media Management

Manage and grow the company's presence across:
  
  

* Instagram
* Facebook
* LinkedIn
* Pinterest
* TikTok

Responsibilities include:
  
  

* Creating monthly social media content calendars across markets
* Writing captions and post copy
* Planning post topics and content themes
* Working with the design team on creatives/collateral
* Publishing and scheduling posts

**KPIs / Success Metrics**

* Develop content around lifestyle, tips, customer stories, convenience and brand messaging

* Ensure consistent messaging across website and social channels

* Monitor engagement and performance across platforms
* Report on social performance monthly

Performance will be measured based on:
  
  

* Social media follower growth

* Gain exposure to global brand-building, content creation and performance-driven marketing
* Work with creative, brand and growth teams to bring innovative social media campaigns to life
* Competitive salary package with comprehensive health insurance coverage
